fine_trace.code: SuccessOrExit(error = otDnsClientQueryRecord(GetInstancePtr(), recordType, aArgs[1].GetCString(), aArgs[2].GetCString(), &HandleDnsRecordResponse, this, config));
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled CLI name tokens (first label of 63 chars plus 192 chars of dot-separated next labels) are passed into the DNS client record-query API; the record callback is HandleDnsRecordResponse.
The 63-char first label is wire-encoded (length byte + label) and appended to the query message after the QueryInfo header.

The next labels (four labels: 63, 63, 62 and 1 chars) are encoded as a DNS name (total encoded length 258 octets, exceeding the 255-octet wire limit, which is not validated here) and appended to the query message, so the rendered name is 256 chars.

With the attacker-supplied response-timeout of 1 ms and max-tx-attempts of 1, the DNS client timer fires and finalizes the query, invoking the record callback with a Response whose mQuery points to the stored query message.
The CLI callback calls otDnsRecordResponseGetQueryName, which renders the stored query name into the caller's 255-byte stack buffer 'name' (OT_DNS_MAX_NAME_SIZE).

After writing 'L1.L2.L3.L4.' (255 chars) the remaining buffer size is 0, so the next label fails this check and ReadName returns kErrorNoBufs WITHOUT writing a null terminator; the buffer should have had mLabelLength < aLabelLength (room for label plus terminator) to stay terminated.
The kErrorNoBufs error from GetQueryName is discarded; the unterminated 255-byte stack buffer 'name' is treated as a valid C string.
OutputLine formats with %s; vsnprintf scans 'name' for a NUL, finds none inside the 255-byte array and reads past its end - stack-buffer-overflow READ reported in ot::Cli::Utils::OutputLine.
